one_liner: Artifex's C PDF/XPS/EPUB engine; about 2.5x faster text extraction than poppler's pdftotext and 2x faster image extraction than PDFium.
what_it_does: MuPDF is a document library in portable C that parses PDF, XPS, EPUB, MOBI, FB2, CBZ, SVG (subset) and Markdown, renders pages to pixmaps, extracts structured text and images, and edits, redacts and rewrites PDFs. The API is not a drop-in for poppler or PDFium: you create an fz_context, open an fz_document, load pages and run them through a device (draw device for raster output, stext device for text, display list for replay). The mutool command-line tool, mupdf-gl viewer, Java/Android, WASM (mupdf.js) and generated C++/Python/C# wrappers sit on the same core; PyMuPDF is the Python binding used in the benchmark.
how_it_is_fast: Pages are interpreted once into a device call stream, and an fz_display_list can record that stream so it can be replayed for rendering, hit-testing or text extraction without re-parsing the content stream; display lists can be rendered on several threads at once. The rasterizer is a global-edge-list scan converter in fixed point with tunable anti-aliasing (17x15 subsamples at the default 8-bit level, down to 2x2 or none), plus Ghostscript-style any-part-of-pixel and centre-of-pixel edge-buffer converters, and span painters specialised per component count (1, 3, 4 channels, with and without alpha). A shared resource store (256 MB by default) caches decoded images, fonts and glyphs across pages. No explicit SIMD intrinsics appear in the paint code; speed comes from these structural choices.
when_to_use: Bulk text extraction from born-digital PDFs where poppler's pdftotext is the current tool: about 2.5x less total time on the py-pdf suite, with a higher text-quality score (94% versus 90%).
Extracting embedded images in bulk: PyMuPDF's extract_image path took about half PDFium's time across 14 papers (7.3 s versus 14.5 s).
Applications that need one engine for rendering, text, annotations, forms, redaction and PDF rewriting, plus XPS and e-book formats, from C, C++, Python, Java or JavaScript.
Multi-page batch rendering on many cores: record a display list per page on one thread, then rasterise lists on worker threads with cloned contexts.
Projects that can ship under AGPL-3.0 or buy Artifex's commercial licence.
when_not_to_use: Closed-source products or network services that will not release source and will not pay Artifex: AGPL-3.0 applies to the whole linked program.
Text extraction when PDFium is already in use: pypdfium2 ties MuPDF on the same suite (1.591 s versus 1.604 s total) and ranks first on text quality (95% versus 94%).
Drawing your own vector graphics (UI, charts, SVG-like scenes): MuPDF is a document interpreter, not a general 2D canvas; Blend2D, Skia or ThorVG are built for that.

Untrusted PDFs in a privileged process without sandboxing: crafted files keep producing memory-safety CVEs (e.g. CVE-2026-3308, an integer overflow in pdf_load_image_imp leading to a heap out-of-bounds write in 1.27.0).
Sharing one document across threads without your own locking: the docs forbid simultaneous calls on the same context, document or device.

integration.form: static lib (libmupdf.a plus libmupdfthird.a) or shared lib; also prebuilt PyMuPDF wheels, an npm WASM module and Java/Android bindings
integration.dependencies: vendored git submodules: freetype, harfbuzz, libjpeg, openjpeg, jbig2dec, lcms2, zlib, brotli, gumbo-parser, mujs, extract, curl, freeglut, zxing-cpp, zint, cmark-gfm; optional tesseract and leptonica (OCR); system copies selectable
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler with GNU make on Linux, BSD and macOS (default release build -O2); Visual Studio solution on Windows; generated C++ wrappers build with -std=c++14
integration.platforms: Linux, BSDs, macOS, Windows (x86, x64, arm64 configuration), Android, WebAssembly
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe only with a caller-supplied fz_locks_context (FZ_LOCK_ALLOC, FZ_LOCK_FREETYPE, FZ_LOCK_GLYPHCACHE) and one cloned fz_context per thread; a document, context or device must never be used by two threads at once, but display lists can be rendered concurrently.

gotchas: C errors are setjmp/longjmp exceptions (fz_try, fz_always, fz_catch); locals modified inside fz_try need fz_var(), and C++ callers should use the generated mupdf:: wrappers, which convert them into C++ exceptions and handle reference counting.

Harness flaw in py-pdf/benchmarks (read this session): PyMuPDF's get_text is called with its default sort=False (no reading-order re-synthesis), while pdftotext runs in its default mode without -raw as a separate process after the PDF is written to a temp file, so the tools do different text work and poppler also pays process start-up; the startup share is at most about 0.04 s per document (the smallest pdftotext timing is 0.037 s) and cannot close the gap on large files (GeoTopo 0.308 s versus 0.999 s, 1707.09725 0.190 s versus 0.765 s).

py-pdf/benchmarks cache.json is keyed by library name, not version, and has_doc skips any document that already has a quality score, so timings survive version bumps unless the cache is cleared; HISTORY.md reports 'Speed: no change' for PyMuPDF 1.26.1 to 1.28.2, which the public files cannot distinguish from a stale row. Each cell is a single time.time() run with no warm-up.

The image-extraction comparison is not output-checked: PyMuPDF returns each xref's image in its stored format via extract_image, while the pypdfium2 path calls PdfImage.extract per page object and names every file .jpg; image counts and bytes are never compared.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MuPDF when the input is a PDF, XPS or e-book that must be parsed and rendered or mined for text; the catalogued siblings (Blend2D, Skia-class rasterizers, ThorVG, AGG) draw paths you supply and do not interpret PDF. For drawing your own vector scenes, Blend2D remains the faster general-purpose CPU rasterizer.
verified_claims_summary: py-pdf/benchmarks (independent, BSD-3-Clause harness) on an Intel Core i7-6700HQ timed 14 born-digital PDFs once each through Python: PyMuPDF 1.28.2 text extraction totalled 1.604 s against 4.008 s for the Poppler 24.02.0 pdftotext binary (about 2.5x, derived from page data) and 1.591 s for pypdfium2 5.13.0 (a tie), and image extraction 7.333 s against 14.523 s for pypdfium2 (about 2x, derived from page data); compiler and flags are unstated (prebuilt wheels and a distro binary). Rendering speed is not measured there; the only rendering numbers found are first-party: PyMuPDF's Appendix 4 (367 s versus 646 s for XPDF pdftopng at 150 DPI) and, snippet only, an Artifex-authored PDF Days 2021 survey (Ghent file at 600 dpi: MuPDF 5.4-9.2 s, Poppler 17.6 s, PDFium 37.5 s).
status_note: Actively developed by Artifex (1.28 adds Markdown input, a new options API and checked arithmetic; last commit 2026-10-06 on the GitHub mirror of Artifex's own git server, bugs tracked on bugs.ghostscript.com); copyable under AGPL-3.0 or a paid commercial licence, and the py-pdf numbers stand as B with harness caveats rather than flaws that invalidate them.
